key_cases.case_name: Berges v. County Court of Douglas County
key_cases.holding: The division held that section 19-3-206's grant of exclusive authority to county attorneys over article 3 proceedings does not strip district attorneys of their authority to criminally prosecute mandatory reporters who willfully fail to report under section 19-3-304.
key_cases.relevance: School officials are among the reporters the division identified as subject to misdemeanor prosecution for willfully violating the reporting duty.
key_cases.quote: section 19-3-304 does not set forth a proceeding under article 3; it simply defines an offense.

key_cases.holding: The division held that the Child Protection Act and the Colorado Governmental Immunity Act can be read together, so that a public-employee mandatory reporter is immune from liability for reporting or failing to report child abuse unless the conduct was willful and wanton, and remanded for a Trinity hearing on that question.
key_cases.relevance: Public and private school employees are express § 19-3-304(2) reporters, and this case fixes both their immunity and the willful-and-wanton exception that a family could plead against them.
key_cases.quote: persons who report child abuse under section 19-3-304 are immune from liability unless their conduct is willful, wanton, and malicious.

mandatory_reporters: Enumerated professionals only — Colorado is not a universal-reporter state — Colo. Rev. Stat. § 19-3-304(2) (C.R.S. 2024); any other person may report voluntarily under § 19-3-304(3)
Physicians and surgeons, including physicians in training
Registered nurses and licensed practical nurses
Hospital personnel engaged in the admission, care, or treatment of patients
Public or private school officials and employees
Social workers and workers in any facility or agency licensed or certified by the state
Commercial film and photographic print processors
Clergy members (not for information learned in a communication privileged under Colo. Rev. Stat. § 13-90-107(1)(c))
Workers in the state department of human services
Officers and agents of the state bureau of animal protection, and animal control officers
Educators providing services through the federal WIC program
Directors, coaches, assistant coaches, and athletic program personnel employed by a private sports organization or program
Registered psychologist, marriage and family therapist, and licensed professional counselor candidates
Officials and employees of a county department of health or of human or social services
Employees of the department of early childhood
